analysis.title: Intelligence weekly #136: Weighing the risk-reward for North Asian tech markets amid 2028 AI capex uncertainty
key_insights: UBS CIO stays constructive on AI as a Transformational Innovation Opportunity. It sees a solid 2027 capex outlook, but visibility into 2028 is lower.
UBS forecasts global AI capex of USD 1.0tr in 2026 (the first year above USD 1tr), USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. That implies growth slowing from about 40% in 2027 to about 8% in 2028.
Risks to 2028 capex growth: higher monetization and return hurdles, tighter financing or refinancing, power and grid constraints, data center permitting delays, and US-China technology restrictions.

Enablers whose earnings and valuations are tied to capacity additions are most exposed to a capex slowdown. These include accelerators, networking, servers, power and cooling. Infrastructure operators and AI adopters may benefit more from better utilization and monetization.
UBS favors established hyperscalers with strong cash generation and the financial capacity to sustain AI investment through a more volatile capex cycle.
In 3Q26 earnings season, 13% of S&P 500 companies quantified AI-driven productivity benefits, but only 3% quantified earnings impacts. UBS expects the benefits to become clearer in 2027.

Hyperscaler capex has exceeded operating cash flow and free cash flow is expected to turn more negative. Hyperscalers increasingly fund spending through debt, equity, leases and supplier-backed financing.

Neoclouds face greater refinancing risk. UBS sees limited risk to aggregate capex because the largest hyperscalers and SpaceX account for about 80% of forecast 2027 spending, against about 8% for neoclouds. It sees selective project delays, not a broad capex downturn.

Post-midterm Democratic gains in states with large planned data center capacity could increase scrutiny of permitting, grid connections, tax incentives, and water and energy use. Already-approved projects are likely to proceed, but some 2028 deployments could shift into 2029.
Tighter review of data center grid connections proposed by Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa could make power a meaningful constraint on AI project timelines.

Limits on Chinese users' remote access to overseas data centers for AI training could curb China's contribution to global compute spending. US restrictions may speed China's compute self-reliance, but domestic capability may not replace overseas advanced chips by 2028.

Shortage-driven memory price hikes accounted for over 50% of the global AI capex increase in 2026. Korean memory makers' 2027 capacity expansion could ease shortages as capex growth moderates, raising the risk of a pricing reversal.
UBS keeps South Korea at Neutral and still favors SK Hynix, which holds the leading position in HBM.
UBS downgrades Taiwan from Attractive to Neutral. Semiconductors and hardware are over 85% of the benchmark, 2027 earnings growth is expected at around 60%, and visibility into 2028 has deteriorated.
Within Taiwan, UBS favors TSMC (foundry), MediaTek (ASIC) and ASE Technology (OSAT) as AI supply-chain leaders.
Effective 1 November 2026, UBS CIO no longer rates equities as Most Preferred or Least Preferred. It now uses a non-rating CIO Selected designation. The selection history table is for reference only.

market_movers.rationale: UBS CIO still favors SK Hynix within a Neutral Korea view because it holds the leading position in HBM. Memory pricing-reversal risk remains.
UBS favors TSMC as the foundry leader within Taiwan, where it moved to Neutral. Its leadership should give resilience as AI spending growth moderates.
UBS favors ASE Technology as the OSAT supplier among Taiwanese AI supply-chain leaders.
UBS favors MediaTek as the Taiwanese ASIC vendor. It has no US listing.

sector_views.rationale: Downgraded from Attractive to Neutral. Semiconductors and hardware are over 85% of the benchmark, and moderating AI capex could hurt spending and earnings expectations beyond 2027.
Memory supply expansion raises the risk of a pricing reversal as AI capex growth normalizes.

sector_views.sector: AI infrastructure enablers (semiconductors, networking, servers, power, cooling)
sector_views.rationale: Earnings and valuations are most tied to capacity additions, so they are most exposed to slower capex growth.
Strong cash generation and financial capacity let them sustain AI investment through a volatile capex cycle. They have multiple monetization channels.

earnings_insights: During 3Q26 earnings season, 13% of S&P 500 companies quantified AI-driven productivity benefits and 3% quantified earnings impacts.
UBS expects Taiwan 2027 earnings growth of around 60% (forecast), but visibility into 2028 has deteriorated.
NVIDIA's latest earnings call pointed to robust AI compute demand, as UBS describes it. No figures are given.
risk_factors: Tighter financing and refinancing conditions, especially for neoclouds
Power and grid constraints and data center permitting delays
Memory pricing reversal as Korean capacity expands in 2027
Taiwan's concentration in semiconductors and hardware, over 85% of the benchmark
geopolitical: Possible limits on Chinese users' remote access to overseas data centers for AI training
Escalating US-China technology restrictions on chips, cloud access and cross-border infrastructure
US post-midterm Democratic gains in states with large planned data center capacity, with possible policy challenges to permitting and grid access
Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa's proposed tighter review of data center grid connections

tension_points.bull_case: Robust compute demand, tight capacity and projects under construction support 2027 spending. UBS forecasts capex of USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, and expects Taiwan 2027 earnings growth of around 60%.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth slows from about 40% in 2027 to about 8% in 2028. Monetization hurdles, tighter financing, power and permitting delays, and US-China restrictions could weigh on spending and on enablers' valuations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Taiwan 2027 earnings expectations could be hit by slower AI investment, normalizing component prices or earnings downgrades.

tension_points.bull_case: Samsung and SK Hynix have dominant HBM and DDR positions and strong pricing power amid shortages.
tension_points.bear_case: Substantial 2027 capacity expansion by Korean memory makers could ease shortages just as AI capex growth moderates, risking a pricing reversal that amplifies the earnings impact.

theme_stances.key_argument: Forecasts imply AI capex growth slowing from about 40% in 2027 to about 8% in 2028, so downside risk needs managing.
Taiwan's 85% weight in semiconductors and hardware leaves it fragile if AI capex moderates, so UBS moves it to Neutral.
theme_stances.evidence: We therefore downgrade Taiwan from Attractive to Neutral
